headline: UK minister reframes carbon capture as "economic infrastructure" for the renewal of British industry
summary: A UK government minister's keynote ("Carbon capture and the renewal of British industry") casts CCUS as "economic infrastructure, not just environmental" and central to rebuilding the industrial base - the government's clearest rhetorical answer to industry warnings on policy and funding delays, in the same week as the CCSA's CCUS 2026 conference and the first five UK CCUS projects reaching financial close in Teesside, the North-West and North Wales.

headline: Indonesia prepares incentives to spur carbon capture at coal-fired power plants
summary: Indonesia is preparing a package of incentives to encourage carbon capture at its coal-fired power plants (PLTU), extending a CCS push hitherto centred on upstream oil-and-gas and dedicated storage licences (Presidential Regulation 14/2024) into the power sector that dominates its grid - a signal that a major Asian coal economy is leaning on CCS retrofit rather than only early plant retirement.
organisations: Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources (Indonesia)
co2crc_note: Indonesia is a priority APAC CCS market and a plausible cross-border storage and partnership counterpart for Australia; a power-sector incentive signal shapes regional CCS demand and storage-hub opportunities.
extractor_note: Incentive package reported as in preparation (not yet detailed or allocated); PerPres 14/2024 and the National Electricity Plan CCS-for-coal roadmap are supporting context. Direct page fetch blocked by egress proxy; date from alerts-ingest metadata.

headline: Japan pushes to move carbon capture from demonstration to a commercial industry
summary: A trade report frames Japan as working to take CCS out of the demonstration phase into a commercial industry - consistent with its roadmap to begin commercial CCS around 2030, the JOGMEC 'Advanced CCS' projects (several built around ship-transported liquefied CO2) advancing toward investment decisions, and the 2024 Act on Carbon Dioxide Storage Business - with knock-on relevance for APAC cross-border CO2 shipping and demand for Australian storage.
co2crc_note: Japan is a central actor in APAC cross-border CO2 shipping and a potential source of stored-CO2 demand for Australian basins; its commercialisation pace directly affects Australian storage-hub prospects.
